overview.text: Anchorage is Alaska’s largest city and lies in Southcentral Alaska at the head of Cook Inlet. The Municipality of Anchorage is a unified home-rule borough, broader than its central city and including communities such as Eagle River, Girdwood and Eklutna. Its modern growth began as headquarters for construction of the Alaska Railroad in 1914–15; the city incorporated in 1920. Anchorage is also associated with the Iditarod Trail Sled Dog Race: downtown hosts the ceremonial start, whose roughly 11-mile route crosses streets, parks and multi-use trails. This ceremonial run is separate from the timed race to Nome.

key_facts.text: Anchorage is Alaska’s largest city and is in the Southcentral region.
The Municipality of Anchorage is a unified home-rule borough that includes communities such as Chugiak, Eagle River, Eklutna and Girdwood.
Anchorage is at the head of Cook Inlet.
The Alaska Railroad construction headquarters helped spur Anchorage’s growth; the city incorporated in 1920.
The Iditarod’s downtown Anchorage ceremonial start follows an approximately 11-mile route, and that segment does not count toward the official race time to Nome.
